item.title: National Guard deployment in D.C. approaches one year
item.description: President Trump's deployment of the National Guard will hit the one year mark next week. The presence of armed, uniformed troops on the street has become increasingly normalized in the capital.

item.title: The daring, 10,000-mile-long journey to circumnavigate the Arctic Ocean
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Captain Matt Rutherford, who is attempting to be the first person to circumnavigate the Arctic Ocean, solo and without any assistance.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Captain Matt Rutherford, who is attempting to be the first person to circumnavigate the Arctic Ocean, solo and without any assistance.

item.title: How a delivery driver and poet won one of China's highest honors in literature
item.description: Wang Jibing, a writer and delivery driver, has won one of China's most prestigious award for poetry. Professor Eileen Cheng-yin Chow of Duke University explains why his work has had such huge impact.

item.title: Science reporter on how evidence based reporting can be a parent's best friend
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz talks to reporter Maria Godoy about how parents can wade through the noise and opinions to find information to help keep their kids healthy.

item.title: Despite war and strife, millions of Shia Muslims in Iraq gather for sacred pilgrimage
item.description: More than 20 million Shia pilgrims flocked to a shrine city in Iraq this week, including millions of Iranians, despite the wars tearing across the Middle East.
item.content:encoded: More than 20 million Shia pilgrims flocked to a shrine city in Iraq this week, including millions of Iranians, despite the wars tearing across the Middle East.

item.title: Tanker sailors still face danger in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: An agreement over the Strait of Hormuz is still far away. Tim Wilkins, who works for a tanker industry group, says the ships stuck around the waterway are in limbo, and transiting is still dangerous.

item.title: GOP-controlled Senate delivers win for Trump with Blanche confirmation
item.description: The Senate narrowly confirmed former Trump personal attorney Todd Blanche as U.S. Attorney General, a major win for the president's approach to keeping the Justice Department close to the White House.

item.description: President Trump signed two executive orders targeting birthright citizenship and "birth tourism." The latter is an issue that Trump has raised for years.

item.title: The U.S. unexpectedly lost jobs in July
item.description: The U.S. labor market went into reverse last month, as employers cut 23,000 jobs. Job gains for May and June were also revised downward.
